```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A's payer is a business buyer who already pays for this category. Solo therapists pay $49-$99/mo for SimplePractice and $69/mo for TherapyNotes (both prices sourced). A first sale means converting someone from an existing spending habit at a meaningfully higher price than Idea B's ~$4/mo consumer subscription.",
    "Idea A's demand evidence is more specific and comes from more independent sources. Several Reddit threads and a competitor's aggregated interviews describe incumbents as 'overkill' and 'really expensive for what it offers', and the brief notes that SimplePractice has raised prices annually since its PE acquisition, which is pushing some therapists to look elsewhere. Idea B's demand rests on one conditional app review and one builder's personal motivation.",
    "Idea A has a reachable, concentrated channel for winning a first customer by hand: r/therapists, where EHR comparison discussion already happens. That suits a 90-day goal of one paying customer. Idea B depends on either paid installs at ~$3.60 iOS CPI against a ~$4/mo price, or organic indie channels that have no evidence of converting.",
    "Idea B's strongest evidence is negative. Artifact was well funded, well staffed, and award-winning, yet shut down because the market opportunity was too small. At least five free or freemium near-clones are live, and the core feature is being absorbed into free platforms. A solo builder starts behind all of these.",
    "Idea A's main risk is HIPAA compliance: BAAs, a risk assessment, and secure infrastructure, estimated at $8K-$25K in year one. This is a real and costly obstacle but a known, bounded one that can be planned and budgeted. Idea B's core problem, weak willingness to pay against free substitutes, has no comparable fix."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's main willingness-to-pay evidence is a single Syft Play Store review: 'Revert the UI back and I'll pay. Until then I'm deleting this and using inoreader.' It is one anonymous, conditional statement from a user who was leaving the app. The brief's claim that solo-built clones are 'already monetizing small niches with $4/month price points' cites only list prices, with no revenue or subscriber evidence.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. Neither brief shows evidence of a new entrant actually winning paying customers. Idea A's demand evidence centers on price complaints, and its own brief admits none of the sourced complaints describe an unmet need for a minimal notes+reminders tool. The HIPAA compliance burden could realistically push a first paid customer past 90 days for one person. Some of A's competitor prices (TheraSoft, TheraFocus) are unsourced. A is picked because its payers already spend money in the category and show documented dissatisfaction, while B's evidence points mostly toward low willingness to pay."
}
```
